raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Reverts #62475 to unblock the ROCm 10.0 nightly while we pick a proper fix.

## Claims

- Fixes the `Build release image - x86_64 - ROCm 10.0` nightly failure: the `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link fails with `mold: relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against .eh_frame out of range`.

## Validation

Built and linked the full `_rocm_C` with this revert in the ROCm 10.0 CI build image (same compiler, mold, 9 release archs, `RelWithDebInfo`): link succeeds.

## Details

**Root cause:** `_rocm_C`'s embedded GPU code (`.hip_fatbin`) was already ~1.94 GiB, ~80% of it uncompressed GPU debug info. Splitting attention into 12 files duplicates that debug info per file and pushed the library past the 2 GiB relocation limit. This revert only gets us back under it, with ~64 MB of headroom.

**Alternatives** (each lets us reland #62475). Measured on one attention file, 9 archs:

| Option | GPU code size | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Today | 137 MiB | | |
| `-Xarch_device -g0` | 36 MiB (−74%) | Simple; ~20% faster compile | No GPU debug info (no kernel source debugging, no source lines for GPU faults) |
| `--offload-compress` | 4.9 MiB (−96%) | Keeps full debug info; output unchanged after decompression; smaller wheel | Decompression at module load (not yet measured on GPU); needs ROCm ≥ 6.2 |

Either option is a one-line CMake change. Both make every HIP object miss sccache once, so the next nightly after either lands is a cold build.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@@ -1493,61 +1493,11 @@ if(VLLM_GPU_LANG STREQUAL "HIP")
   #
   # _rocm_C extension
   #
-  # The paged attention *instantiations* are split over one translation unit
-  # per (dtype, kv-cache dtype, head size) combination: compiling them all in a
-  # single file serializes ~10 min of device code generation onto one core.
-  # attention_dispatch.cu only holds the runtime dispatch, attention_kernels.cuh
-  # the kernels and launchers. A file listed here is dead weight unless
-  # attention_dispatch.cu also dispatches its entry point (guarded below).
   set(VLLM_ROCM_EXT_SRC
     "csrc/rocm/torch_bindings.cpp"
     "csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu"
     "csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h64_f16_auto.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_f16_auto.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h64_bf16_auto.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_bf16_auto.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h64_f16_fp8_f16.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_f16_fp8_f16.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h64_f16_fp8_fp8.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_f16_fp8_fp8.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h64_bf16_fp8_f16.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_bf16_fp8_f16.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h64_bf16_fp8_fp8.cu"
-    "csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h128_bf16_fp8_fp8.cu")
-
-  # Each attention_paged_attn_*.cu file below instantiates one kernel set and
-  # exposes it as one entry point. That entry point is only reachable if
-  # paged_attention() in csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu names it in one of its
-  # ATTN_HEAD_SWITCH() calls (the dispatch arms); otherwise the file is compiled
-  # and linked unnecessarily. Fail at configure time instead.
-  file(READ "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu" _attn_dispatch)
-  string(FIND "${_attn_dispatch}" "#define ATTN_HEAD_SWITCH" _attn_arms_pos)
-  if (_attn_arms_pos EQUAL -1)
-    message(FATAL_ERROR
-      "csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu no longer defines ATTN_HEAD_SWITCH; "
-      "update the instantiation guard in CMakeLists.txt accordingly.")
-  endif()
-  string(SUBSTRING "${_attn_dispatch}" ${_attn_arms_pos} -1 _attn_arms)
-  foreach (_attn_src ${VLLM_ROCM_EXT_SRC})
-    if (_attn_src MATCHES "^csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_.*\\.cu$")
-      file(READ "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/${_attn_src}" _attn_tu)
-      string(REGEX MATCHALL "ATTN_ENTRY\\([A-Za-z0-9_]+\\)" _attn_entries
-        "${_attn_tu}")
-      foreach (_attn_entry ${_attn_entries})
-        string(REGEX REPLACE "ATTN_ENTRY\\((.*)\\)" "\\1" _attn_name
-          "${_attn_entry}")
-        if (NOT _attn_arms MATCHES "${_attn_name}[,)]")
-          message(FATAL_ERROR
-            "${_attn_src} instantiates ${_attn_name}, but "
-            "csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu never dispatches it: the file "
-            "would be compiled and linked for nothing. Add it to one of the "
-            "ATTN_HEAD_SWITCH() calls in paged_attention().")
-        endif()
-      endforeach()
-    endif()
-  endforeach()
+    "csrc/rocm/attention.cu")
   set(VLLM_ROCM_EXT_FLAGS ${VLLM_GPU_FLAGS})
 
   # skinny_gemms*.cu are built on gfx9/gfx11 ISA (MFMA, dot2/dot4, legacy

@@ -153,10 +153,7 @@ class RocmAttentionBackend(AttentionBackend):
     def get_supported_kernel_block_sizes(kv_cache_spec=None) -> list[int | MultipleOf]:
         # ROCM paged attention native C++ kernel only supports block sizes 16 and 32
         # due to shared memory (LDS) constraints on AMD GPUs.
-        # The (head_size, block_size) pairs that have a native kernel are enumerated
-        # by csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_<head>_<dtype>_<kv>.cu, each of which
-        # instantiates ATTN_LAUNCH from csrc/rocm/attention_kernels.cuh; the runtime
-        # gate is use_rocm_custom_paged_attention() in vllm/platforms/rocm.py.
+        # See csrc/rocm/attention.cu CALL_CUSTOM_LAUNCHER_BLK macro.
         # However, vLLM allows support for any multiple of 16 via the Triton path.
         # As addressed in PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31380,
         # non-standard models (like qwen3-next with block_size 544, or qwen3_5
@@ -166,9 +163,6 @@ def get_supported_kernel_block_sizes(kv_cache_spec=None) -> list[int | MultipleO
 
     @classmethod
     def get_supported_head_sizes(cls) -> list[int]:
-        # Head sizes with a native ROCm kernel are only 64 and 128 (see
-        # csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_h{64,128}_*.cu); the remaining entries are
-        # served by the Triton fallback selected in use_rocm_custom_paged_attention().
         return [32, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256]
 
     @classmethod
